observation: Rocky uses one of his metal blocks to wave at the narrator upon emerging from the airlock.
Rocky manipulates metal controls through his xenonite shell using magnets, while remaining encased in his geodesic ball.
Rocky shifts around within his geodesic ball when encountering new objects, appearing to use sonar for better spatial awareness.
Rocky points toward the 3-D printer with one of his metal blocks, then settles on it as his point of interest.
Rocky expresses sadness about sleeping alone, stating "I bring my things into you ship. Release tunnel. You make you ship spin for science."
Rocky uses multiple metal blocks as magnets to anchor and move his geodesic ball across surfaces, stabilizing it during manipulation tasks.
Rocky hangs out in his ball, magnetically attached to the wall.
Rocky uses magnets from inside his ball to climb along the pile of duffel bags and rearrange them.
Rocky makes a turning motion with two arms to demonstrate how to rotate the tunnel.
trigger: narrator asks how to detach the tunnel
interpretation: demonstrating the action required to rotate the tunnel

observation: Rocky wiggles his carapace when explaining the device broke off.
interpretation: attempting to explain or emphasize the cause of the breakage

observation: Rocky's carapace slumps down with elbows above his breathing holes, indicating sadness.
Rocky dips his carapace significantly when discussing his failures, lower than usual.
Rocky raises his carapace slightly after the narrator offers encouragement.
Rocky wiggles a claw when stating the average Eridian lifespan.
Rocky's voice drops to a low tone when discussing his repeated failures.
Rocky floats off when a duffel bag becomes loose and calls the narrator to put him back.
interpretation: indicating reliance on the narrator for reattachment
